Consult Summary:
Young woman with sudden left-sided throbbing headache beginning midday today, preceded by visual aura and associated with photophobia and vomiting; features consistent with migraine with aura. Reassured regarding fears of brain tumor; provided abortive treatment advice, headache diary, and red-flag safety-netting.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Suspected migraine with aura
- Onset today at ~12 PM; second similar episode within one month (prior episode lasted ~2 days).
- Symptoms: left-sided throbbing headache, visual “zig-zag” lines and blurred vision prior to pain, photophobia (wearing sunglasses indoors), nausea with two episodes of vomiting, pain worsens with head/neck movement.
- No fever, rash, focal neurologic deficits, speech disturbance, limb weakness, balance issues, head trauma, or breathlessness.
- Examination findings/vitals: not documented.
- Differential discussed: brain tumor (patient concern) and meningitis (clinician ruled out).
- Impression: migraine with aura.

Issue 2: Health anxiety related to fear of brain cancer
- Triggered by friend’s mother’s recent brain tumor death and online searching.
- Reassurance provided; advised on red-flag symptoms and follow-up.

Issue 3: Work-related stress and lifestyle factors
- High-pressure fashion industry role; currently “really stressful.”
- Lives alone; does not exercise; no smoking or alcohol.
- Stress may contribute to headache frequency.

Medications:
- Microgynon oral contraceptive pill – dose/route/frequency not documented (taken for 3 months).
- Recommended PRN: Paracetamol, Co-codamol, Ibuprofen, or Naproxen – doses/routes/frequencies not documented (patient to use for acute migraine).

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- None reported.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Occupation: fashion industry; high job stress.
- Non-smoker; denies alcohol use.
- No regular exercise.

Preventative History:
- No information on cervical screening, mammogram, colon screening, vaccinations, skin or eye checks, etc.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not recorded.
- Neurologic, cardiovascular, ENT exams: not recorded.

Plan:
- Treat current migraine with advised analgesics/anti-inflammatories.
- Begin headache diary to identify triggers and monitor frequency.
- Consider prophylactic migraine medication if headaches become more frequent or disabling; to be reviewed at follow-up next week.
- Safety-net: return immediately if headache worsens, persists >2–3 days, fails to respond to medication, or if new symptoms (neck stiffness, visual changes, limb weakness, speech changes) develop.
- Follow-up appointment planned in one week; sooner if red-flag symptoms occur.
- Discuss ongoing stress management and lifestyle modification at next visit.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: allergies, medication doses/routes/frequencies, vitals, physical examination findings.  
● No internal conflicts identified.  
● Transcript quality: clear; minimal background noise; no inaudible sections.
